noConnection.title: No active connection
noConnection.body: Pick or add a profile above, then Connect. First connect to a profile triggers the discovery probe automatically.

common.anotherOperationInProgress: Another operation is already in progress.

toasts.requiredError: Name, host, and user are required.
toasts.keyAuthSuccess: Key auth set up — future connects won't need the password.

newProfileDialog.descNew: SSH connection details. New profiles start on password auth — once connected, use "Set up key auth" to switch to a key so you won't need to retype the password.
newProfileDialog.descEdit: Auth method, saved key, and discovery stay as they are — only these fields change.

deleteDialog.title: Delete {{name}}?
deleteDialog.desc: Removes the profile and its cached discovery info. Any saved password or key in the OS keyring is left alone. This can't be undone from here.

passwordDialog.title: Connect to {{name}}
passwordDialog.desc: Password for {{user}}@{{host}}. Never stored unless you later enable "save password".

keyAuthDialog.title: Set up key auth for {{name}}?
keyAuthDialog.desc: Generates a new SSH key (kept locally, never sent anywhere but this host's <1>~/.ssh/authorized_keys</1>) and switches this profile to key auth. You won't need to type the password again.

discoveryConfirm.title: Confirm what was found
discoveryConfirm.descPrefix: Nothing is saved until you confirm — SPEC §8. Detected OS:
discoveryConfirm.manualUnitPlaceholder: No service auto-detected — enter a systemd unit name manually
discoveryConfirm.pickServicePlaceholder: Pick the real Core Keeper service…
discoveryConfirm.manualWorldsPathPlaceholder: No worlds dir found — enter the path manually

toasts.pickServiceError: Pick (or enter) a service before confirming.
toasts.pickWorldsPathError: Pick (or enter) a worlds path before confirming.

logDrawer.title: Live log
logDrawer.desc: Polling every {{seconds}}s — not a true -f stream, but close enough to watch along.

push.title: Push a world
push.desc: Stops the live server, backs up the current world, swaps yours in, restarts, and verifies — auto-rolls back on any failure. No guarantee against data loss — keep your own backups.
push.otherOpBanner: A {{operation}} is in progress — finish or wait before starting a push.
push.pugbackupNote: ↳ Core Keeper's own rolling backup for this slot, found alongside the main file — included automatically, both travel together.
push.unassignedNote: This file's name doesn't say which slot it belongs to — name it N.world.gzip (N being the slot number) to have that detected automatically, or just pick the slot below (defaults to 0).
push.confirmDesc: This stops the live Core Keeper server, backs up the current world (dated, restorable), copies yours in, restarts, and verifies. On any failure it automatically restores the backup and restarts the server.

stepper.failedBanner: Rolled back — server restart was attempted automatically.

pull.title: Pull a world
pull.desc: Stops the live server just long enough to copy a consistent world, restarts immediately, then lets you save it locally. No guarantee against data loss — keep your own backups.
pull.noWorlds: No worlds found on the server.
pull.otherOpBanner: A {{operation}} is in progress — finish or wait before starting a pull.
pull.confirmDesc: Briefly stops the live Core Keeper server to copy a consistent world file, then restarts it immediately. Nothing on the server is modified.

toasts.success: World {{slot}} downloaded — pick where to save it.

stepper.failedBanner: Failed — a restart was attempted automatically regardless.

worldLibrary.title: World library
worldLibrary.desc: What's live on the server, and every dated backup this app has made. Restoring is the same safe envelope as a push — no guarantee against data loss, keep your own backups.
worldLibrary.otherOpBanner: A {{operation}} is in progress — finish or wait before starting a restore.
worldLibrary.noWorlds: No worlds found on the server.
worldLibrary.noBackupsYet: — none yet; your first push or restore creates one.
worldLibrary.confirmDesc: Stops the live server, backs up whatever's currently live (so this itself is undoable), copies this backup into place, restarts, and verifies.

stepper.failedBanner: Rolled back — a safety backup was restored and the server restarted automatically.

terminal.title: Terminal
terminal.desc: A real shell over SSH — same trust level as ssh root@host, not sandboxed.
terminal.otherOpBanner: A {{operation}} is in progress — commands run here can race its own stop/start sequence. Best to wait it out.
terminal.noActiveSession: No active session. Click "Start terminal session" to open a real shell.

confirm1.title: Clear the entire audit log?
confirm1.desc: Deletes every session, event, SSH command, error, file operation, and backup record — all of it, not just what's currently filtered. This cannot be undone.

confirm2.title: No, like — are you REALLY sure?
confirm2.desc: This is the digital equivalent of shredding the black box right before the NTSB shows up. Every "why did the server die at 3am" mystery you could've solved — gone. Every rollback you were quietly proud of — never happened. The audit log doesn't get better with age, it just dies, and you're the one holding the knife. Last chance to back away slowly.
confirm2.confirm: Yes. Do it. Let it go quietly.

about.title: World Keeper
about.versionDesc: Version {{version}} — MIT licensed. A homelab tool for managing a Core Keeper dedicated server's worlds over SSH; see the project's GitHub repo for source and docs.

commandReference.title: Command reference
commandReference.desc: Every remote command this app can run, grouped by what you'd be doing when it runs. Shows placeholders like <worldsPath> until you're connected, then the real values for this server.

disclaimer.title: Before you start
disclaimer.body1: This tool stops your Core Keeper server and overwrites world files on a remote host you control. It backs up before every destructive step and rolls back on failure — but it's a homelab tool, not a certified backup product, and it comes with <1>no guarantee against data loss or corruption</1>.
disclaimer.body2: Keep your own independent backups of anything you can't afford to lose.
